titre.sous: will, will be doing, will have done

bulles.texte: Can I call you at three?
No, I **will be flying** to Lagos.

lignes.exemple: We **are going to hire** two people.

by.titre: by + a future time = will have done

bulles.texte: **By** next Friday, she **will have sent** all the invoices.

piege.titre: No will after when, as soon as, before

bulles.texte: I will call you when I __will arrive__.
I will call you when I **arrive**.

q.lu: **By** the end of the year, the firm ------- three stores.

etapes.texte: **by** + a future time: will have + participle
After __when, as soon as, before, until__: present, never will

phrases.texte: Will, plus the verb, is for a prediction or a decision: sales will rise next year.
phrases.dit: Will, plus the verb, is for a prediction, or a decision: sales will rise next year.

phrases.texte: Be going to is for a plan: we are going to hire two people.
phrases.dit: Be going to, is for a plan: we are going to hire two people.

phrases.texte: Will be, plus -ing, is for an action in progress at a future moment: at three, I will be flying.
phrases.dit: Will be, plus ing, is for an action in progress at a future moment: at three, I will be flying.

phrases.texte: Will have, plus the past participle, is for an action finished before a future moment: by June, we will have finished.
The clue is the word by, with a future time. By next Friday, she will have sent all the invoices.
phrases.dit: The clue is the word by, with a future time. By next Friday, she will have sent all the invoices.

phrases.texte: One trap. After when, as soon as and before, we do not use will.
phrases.dit: One trap. After when, as soon as, and before, we do not use will.

phrases.texte: We use the present: I will call you when I arrive.
Now, a TOEIC question. By the end of the year, the firm, blank, three stores.
A: opens. B: opened. C: is opening. D: will have opened.
phrases.dit: Answer A. opens. Answer B. opened. Answer C. is opening. Answer D. will have opened.

phrases.texte: The time expression is: by the end of the year. It is a future moment, and the action is finished before it.
So the present, the past and the continuous are wrong.
D is correct: by the end of the year, the firm will have opened three stores.
Three steps. One: find the time expression first.
Two: by, plus a future time, goes with will have and the past participle.
Three: after when, as soon as, before and until, use the present, never will.
